newsitem.title: USA: Fieldcrest Cannon posts loss after $4.5 million charge.
newsitem.headline: Fieldcrest Cannon posts loss after $4.5 million charge.

text.p: Struggling textiles maker Fieldcrest Cannon Inc. posted a higher loss for the third quarter Wednesday after taking a $4.5 million charge for closing a unit and laying off 750 workers.
The company said it had a net loss for the three months ended Sept. 30 of $2.7 million, or 43 cents a share, compared with a net loss of $15,000, or 13 a share, a year ago.
Fieldcrest Cannon, which is based Kannapolis, N.C., said its sales improved slightly to $285.2 million from $280.5 million.

The company, which makes and markets home furnishing products under the Fieldcrest, Royal Velvet, St. Marys, Sure Fit and private brand labels, said the charge stemmed from its previously announced deal to sell some of the assets of its blanket division to Pillowtex Corp. and layoff workers.
"The company is liquidating the remaining assets, closing the blanket division facilities in Eden, N.C., and reducing its work force by approximately 750 employees," it said in a statement.

Chairman James Fitzgibbons cited a number of items that weighed on earnings -- higher cotton costs, $1.7 million of equipment relocation and employee training costs related to closing two towel facilities, and higher general and administrative costs.
In the Pillowtex deal, announced this month, Fieldcrest Cannon agreed to sell certain blanket division inventories and equipment to Pillowtex Corp. for $30 million in cash.
Proceeds from the sale of the Blanket Division assets will be used to reduce debt and for reinvestment in Fieldcrest Cannon's core businesses, Fitzgibbons said.

The transaction includes a long-term trademark license royalty agreement under which Pillowtex will sell blankets and throws, bed pillows and mattress pads with Fieldcrest Cannon's brands and other marks.
Fieldcrest Cannon's stock added 50 cents to $13.625 in late trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
